scenes.text: Scientists think goosebumps are a leftover from when our ancestors had fur.
Tiny muscles at the base of each hair pull it upright.
On a furry animal, that puffs up the fur to trap warm air.
It also makes animals look bigger and scarier, like a porcupine raising its quills.
It's run by your fight or flight system, which is why fear, awe, or great music can trigger it too.
But with so little body hair, our goosebumps barely do anything.
What gives you goosebumps every time?

title: Why you get goosebumps (it's a fur thing) 😱
caption: Goosebumps come from tiny muscles that make each hair stand up. Furry animals use it to stay warm and look bigger; for us, scientists think it's mostly an evolutionary leftover. 😱
